como.cinturaHombre: Level with your navel, standing, belly relaxed. Measure at the end of a normal breath out, without sucking in.
como.cinturaMujer: At the narrowest point, between your navel and breastbone. If it isn’t clear, measure a few times and keep the smallest.
como.cuello: Just below the Adam’s apple, tape straight around the neck, chin forward, shoulders down. Snug: self-measured necks tend to read large.
como.cadera: At the widest part of your buttocks, seen from the side, feet together.
como.brazo: Halfway between the tip of your shoulder and your elbow, arm relaxed at your side.
como.pecho: At the middle of your breastbone, tape under your arms, after breathing out.
como.muslo: Halfway between the crease of your groin and the top of your kneecap.

consejos: A tape that doesn’t stretch, on bare skin.
Standing, feet together, arms at your sides, relaxed.
Keep the tape level with the floor: a mirror helps.
At the end of a normal breath out: don’t suck in.
Always at the same time of day, before eating and after the bathroom.
Measure twice; if they differ by more than 1 cm, a third time, and write down the average.
cuerpo.usaHombre: The estimate uses your waist and neck, with your height. The other measurements help you follow your progress.
cuerpo.usaMujer: The estimate uses your waist, hips and neck, with your height. The other measurements help you follow your progress.
cuerpo.aviso: This is an estimate from your measurements, not a measurement: a lab scan (DEXA) could read 3 or 4 points higher or lower. It’s less precise with very little fat, a lot of muscle or a lot of fat, and it doesn’t apply during pregnancy or under 18. Measure the same way every time and watch the trend.
cuerpo.comoSeEstimaHombre: With the US Navy method (Hodgdon and Beckett, 1984): body density comes from your waist minus your neck and your height, and body fat from the Siri equation. The range is the estimate plus and minus how much it changes if the tape shifts 1 cm at the waist and half a centimetre at the neck, rounded to whole points. With very little or a lot of fat, it opens one more point on each side.
cuerpo.comoSeEstimaMujer: With the US Navy method (Hodgdon and Beckett, 1984): body density comes from your waist plus your hips minus your neck and your height, and body fat from the Siri equation. The range is the estimate plus and minus how much it changes if the tape shifts 1 cm at the waist and hips and half a centimetre at the neck, rounded to whole points. With very little or a lot of fat, it opens one more point on each side.

progreso.ritmoTexto: {pct}% of your weight a week: about {kg} {unidad}.
progreso.objetivoNota: When you change your goal, your targets change from today, using the expenditure Moss has been measuring.
progreso.pesoMetaNota: It shows whether you’re on track and when you’d get there. Targets come from your goal and pace.
progreso.controlListo: The week already has what it needs: the check-in will measure your expenditure and adjust your targets.
progreso.controlFalta: The check-in needs at least 4 logged days and one weigh-in in the week. Without them, your targets stay as they are.
progreso.diaDelControlNota: That day, when you open Moss, the check-in measures the week before. If you don’t open the app that day, it runs next time.
progreso.controlTexto: The check-in measured an expenditure of about {gasto} kcal a day. Moss takes it in gradually: the estimate went from {antes} to {ahora} kcal.

metas.mossTexto: Moss adjusts them every week from your weight and what you eat.
metas.aManoTexto: You set them. Moss keeps measuring your expenditure, but doesn't change them.

equilibrada: Protein by body weight, at least 27% fat and the rest carbs.
bajaEnGrasas: Fat at 20%: more room for carbs.
bajaEnCarbohidratos: A quarter of calories from carbs and the rest from fat.

metas.semanaTexto: More on the days you pick and a bit less on the rest. The week adds up the same: carbs move.

progreso.controlEnCurso: The check-in needs at least 4 logged days and one weigh-in in the week. There are {n} days left: if you keep logging, that’s enough.
progreso.ejemplo: This is sample data: once you log your weight (or connect Health) and finish the questionnaire, yours shows up.
progreso.sinMedidas: No measurements yet. With your waist and neck (and hips, for women), Moss estimates your body fat.
progreso.gastoInicial: Estimated from your answers. Each weekly check-in measures it from your weight and what you eat.
progreso.sinBalance: Log what you eat for a few days to see your balance.

limites.piso: Not below {n} kcal a day: that's less than your body needs to work.
limites.imc: The lowest goal weight for your height is {n} {unidad}: a BMI of 18.5.

sueno.horas: Fell asleep at {desde}, woke up at {hasta}
sueno.incompleta: This night looks incomplete: you slept much less than usual and woke up early. Did your watch run out of battery? You can leave it out.
sueno.etapasEstimadas: Stages are the watch’s estimate: it gets them right much less often than how long you slept.
sueno.sinRelojTexto: Your watch didn’t record this night (out of battery, or not wearing it?). There’s only the iPhone’s time in bed, which measures phone use, not sleep: it doesn’t count for anything.
sueno.sinNadaTexto: There’s no data for this night. It isn’t filled in: it stays out of averages and debt.
sueno.habitosPendientes: That day’s sleep habits stay pending: you can mark them yourself.
sueno.sinCalidad: Without the watch there’s no quality: it needs to know how long you slept.
comoCalidad: It’s a Moss number, from 0 to 100, in three parts. It isn’t Apple’s Sleep Score: Apple doesn’t share it with other apps, so they may not match.
Duration (50): how long you slept against what you need ({necesidad}). 4 hours scores 0, and reaching it scores 50.

Timing (30): how far your sleep and wake times moved from your usual ones (the median of your last two weeks). Up to half an hour scores everything; an hour and a half or more, nothing. With fewer than 5 nights it’s left out and the total is rescaled.
Continuity (20): minutes awake between falling asleep and waking up (full up to 20, none from 60) and awakenings of 5 minutes or more (full with one, none with four).
Stages, time in bed and heart rate aren’t included: the watch measures them less accurately.
sueno.regularidadTexto: From {n} of the last 14 nights. The ± is how much your time moves from night to night: up to half an hour is very regular. The weekend compares the middle of your Friday and Saturday nights with the rest, assuming you don’t work those days.
sueno.deudaDe: short of what you need ({necesidad} a night)
sueno.deudaTexto: What you were short of what you need each night over the last two weeks, counting recent nights more, minus what you slept extra (up to 2 hours a night). Naps count; nights without data neither add nor subtract.
sueno.vitalesTexto: The average while you slept, against the median of your previous nights (7 are needed). The watch measures variability only a few times a night: it’s the least precise. Resting heart rate is for the whole day.
sueno.fuentesTexto: Moss uses a single source per night: the one you choose in Profile › Devices or, if not, the one that best tells sleep from wake. It never adds two together. Without a watch or a ring, it estimates the night with your phone. If a night is missing, it stays grey: nothing is made up.
sueno.noMedico: Moss isn’t a medical device. If you’re worried about your sleep, talk to a doctor.
sueno.ejemplo: These are sample nights: yours show up once you connect Health or after your first night with Moss.

manana.pregunta: How did you sleep last night?
manana.nota: It counts in recovery together with the watch's quality and, without a watch, it is the night's quality.
manana.sinProponer: What time did you fall asleep and wake up?

sueno.sinCalidadEstimada: Moss isn’t sure about this night: confirm it or change it and the quality shows up.
sueno.estimadaTexto: Without a watch, Moss estimates it from your steps, your phone’s motion and when you use the app.
sueno.rango: Between {a} and {b} falling asleep, and between {c} and {d} waking up.
sueno.sinRelojEtapas: Without a watch there are no stages or awakenings: with a watch or a ring, Moss measures them.

movimiento.texto: Without a watch, it helps tell when you fell asleep and woke up. It never leaves your phone.

sueno.fuentesSinReloj: With a watch or a ring, Moss measures instead of estimating. What each one sends is in Profile › Devices.

pocoSueno.texto: Over the last two weeks you slept less than 6 hours a night. If it continues, it's worth talking to a doctor.
pocoSueno.nota: It's an estimate from Moss, not a diagnosis.

privacidadTexto: Your data is yours. Moss stores what you log, your answers, your weight and your nights on your phone and, with your account, on its server, for your other devices. It doesn't sell or share them, show ads or track you.

From Health, Moss reads steps, sleep, water, mindful minutes, weight, age, sex and height. With your account, your weight, birth year, sex, height and which habits you completed are uploaded; Health's steps and sleep stay on your phone. Moss doesn't write to Health.
Meal photos stay on your phone. When you scan a code that isn't in Moss, Open Food Facts is asked about that code only.
If you choose to, what you search for and don't find is sent without your name; so is a mistake you report. You can export everything as CSV and delete your data or your account here.
perfil.recordatoriosTexto: A little after your usual time, and only if you haven’t logged that meal yet. If you don’t open Moss for a week, they stop on their own.
perfil.recordatoriosSinPermiso: To remind you, Moss needs permission for notifications: turn it on in the iPhone’s Settings.
perfil.calidadTexto: Automatic chooses for your iPhone and steps down by itself if the sky stutters. Low uses less battery.

aparatos.arriba: Moss works with just the iPhone and gets better with a watch or a ring. Everything comes through Health.
aparatos.tuyos: The ones that write your sleep
aparatos.automaticaTexto: The most precise one each night.
aparatos.varios: If you use more than one, Moss takes one per night, the one you choose, and never adds them together.

iphone.texto: With just the iPhone, Moss estimates when you slept from your steps, your phone’s motion and when you use the app, and asks you in the morning to confirm it. With a watch or a ring, it’s measured.

appleWatch.texto: How long and when you slept, with stages and naps; at night, your heart rate, heart rate variability and breathing; wrist temperature from Series 8 on, and blood oxygen on the models that measure it.

oura.texto: How long and when you slept, with stages, and the night’s heart rate and breathing. Variability and temperature stay in the Oura app. Open it every day so the data comes through.

whoop.texto: How long and when you slept, without stages, and the night’s resting heart rate, breathing and blood oxygen. Stages and variability stay in the WHOOP app.

garmin.texto: How long and when you slept, with stages, your heart rate and steps. Open Garmin Connect so it sends the data. Variability and Body Battery stay in Garmin.

google.texto: With a Fitbit or a Fitbit Air: how long and when you slept, with stages, heart rate, resting heart rate, breathing and blood oxygen. Connect the Google Health app to Health. Variability doesn’t come through.

polar.texto: How long you slept, without stages, your steps and workouts.

withings.texto: Your weight and body composition; with the Sleep Analyzer or a ScanWatch, your sleep too. If you created your account after October 12, 2026, you need Withings+ to send data to Health.

ringconn.texto: How long and when you slept, with stages, and the night’s heart rate and blood oxygen.

ultrahuman.texto: The variability and temperature its app sends to Health.

amazfit.texto: Your steps, heart rate and sleep; the detail depends on the model.

coros.texto: Your heart rate, sleep and steps.

suunto.texto: Your workouts, steps and heart rate; sleep doesn’t reach Health.

samsung.texto: The Pixel Watch, the Galaxy Watch and the Galaxy Ring don’t work with iPhone.

perfil.sinDeficitTexto: Because of pregnancy, breastfeeding or a medical condition: Moss won't suggest eating less than you burn.
perfil.numerosTexto: No calories or grams: just the shapes and the bars.
perfil.mejorarBaseTexto: Without your name: this helps Moss add what is missing.

avisos.dormirTexto: A little before the time to go to bed: the one that lets you sleep what you need, with some of your sleep debt and never more than an hour earlier than usual. Tonight, {hora}.
avisos.dormirSinDatos: A little before the time to go to bed: the one that lets you sleep what you need. Moss needs to know when you wake up: a few nights is enough.
avisos.maximoTexto: Reminders that fall close together ring together, and never more than this a day. If there are too many, bedtime and your habits come first. Each habit's reminder is set in the habit.

perfil.cambiarCuentaTexto: This session closes and you sign in with another account. What’s on this phone is deleted; your data stays in your account.

ascent.bajada: Link the two apps and your sleep and food meet your training.
ascent.conseguir: Don’t have Ascent? Find it on the App Store
ascent.permiso: Linking lets the two apps share your data, and you can undo it in Profile.

hoy.meta: Today’s target: {kcal} kcal and {p} g protein
hoy.reparto: Gym days get {entreno} kcal and rest days {descanso}. The week adds up to {semana}, the same as the check-in.

proteina.techo: Protein stays: it’s already at 2.2 g per kilo, and more doesn’t add muscle.
proteina.chica: Protein stays: the session was half your usual or less.

recuperacion.texto: A daily score from your sleep, your food and your training. Before you train, it tells you whether to go hard or easy.
recuperacion.explicacion: Sleep, 40: how much you slept against what you need, and the night’s quality. Load, 40: what you trained in the previous 3 days against your 4-week average, minus days in a row. Food, 20: yesterday’s protein and whether you ate at least 80% of your target. It’s a guide.

estancamiento.texto: When Ascent sees you’ve stalled on an exercise, Moss adds what changed in your sleep, protein and calories.

frases.sueno: Your best lifts come in the weeks you sleep {horas} or more.
frases.proteina: Your best lifts come in the weeks you hit your protein.
frases.calorias: Your best lifts come in the weeks you eat closer to your expenditure.

estancamiento.nota: It’s a probable cause, not a sure one: it compares your weeks.
estancamiento.juntando: Moss is still gathering information to find the probable cause.
estancamiento.juntandoDetalle: It needs {min} weeks with PRs and {min} without, each with at least {dias} days of food and {dias} nights of sleep. So far, {a} and {b}.
estancamiento.sinDiferencia: There’s no clear difference in your sleep, protein or calories: the probable cause lies elsewhere.

anio.texto: Workouts, PRs, habits, sleep and food from the year, all in one.

peso.texto: Weigh in on either app and it’s logged in both.

calorias.texto: Gym days raise your target and rest days lower it: the week adds up the same.

objetivo.texto: Cutting or bulking in Moss changes what Ascent expects from your strength.

vivo.bajar: Cutting: Ascent doesn’t expect new PRs
vivo.subir: Bulking: Ascent expects you to go up

cuenta.texto: The same friends list in both apps.

proteina.texto: A session bigger than your usual raises that day’s protein.

gimnasio.titulo: Gym lights up on its own
gimnasio.texto: If you log the day in Ascent, the gym star lights up on its own.
gimnasio.vivo: Add “Gym” to your habits and it lights up on its own

rendimiento.texto: What you can expect today, in max strength and in reps, from your sleep, your food and what you trained.
rendimiento.margen: Give or take {n} %: that’s how much it changes from one day to the next.

motivos.despertoAntes: You woke up earlier than usual
motivos.nochesCortas: Two of your last three nights were short
motivos.ayuno: You’re coming in after 8 hours without food
motivos.bajandoRapido: You’re losing more than 1 % a week
motivos.comioPoco: You ate less than 80 % of your calories yesterday
motivos.descarga: You’re coming off a deload week, with the same load
motivos.sinEntrenarlo: You haven’t trained it in {dias} days

rendimiento.sinReloj: From what your phone estimated: a watch would be more precise.
como: Two numbers, in % of your usual: max strength (1 to 3 reps) and reps. Short sleep barely touches max strength and hits reps much harder.
It adds up last night’s sleep (or several short nights in a row), how you said you slept, food (coming in fasted, few carbs, losing fast), muscle fatigue and deloads. Between −15 and +4 %.
Your strength moves about 3 % from one day to the next: that’s why it says “as usual” most days. It isn’t a guarantee.

musculos.texto: Which muscles are rested and which aren’t, from the sets you log in Ascent.
musculos.antes: Before training today, from what you logged in Ascent
musculos.nota: Soreness doesn’t count: strength comes back before soreness goes away.

marca.texto: When your conditions look like the ones of your PRs, it lets you know: you slept well, your muscles rested and you’re close.
marca.en: Good day to try a PR in {ejercicio}
marca.porque: You slept {horas}; {musculos}: {dias} days of rest. Your best recent set is {g} % from your PR.
marca.aciertos: I flagged it {veces} times; you hit a PR in {marcas}.
marca.nota: It’s an estimate, not a promise. If your warm-up feels heavy, save it for another day.
marca.hoyNo: No PR to try today: it lets you know when your conditions look like the ones of your PRs.

mossComparte: How long you slept and how you said you slept
What you eat: calories and protein
ascentComparte: Your workouts, with their sets and your PRs
vincularHoja.nota: Each app keeps its own data. You can unlink them anytime from Profile.

habitos.aManoTexto: You tap the star when you do it.
habitos.saludTexto: It lights up on its own when Health says you got there.
habitos.comidaTexto: It lights up on its own with what you log.

habitos.cambiaLaConstelacion: Days that change how many habits they have move to another constellation.
habitos.mantener: Press and hold a star to edit its habit.

sugeridos.texto: 3 to 5 to start: they make your first constellation. The food ones light up on their own with what you log.
sugeridos.despues: Later you can add, change or archive each one.

aviso.texto: It rings on the days you choose, and not if it's already done. Moss groups the ones that fall close together and never goes over the daily maximum (Profile › Reminders).

habitos.minimo: You need at least 3 habits: the constellation changes with how many there are.
